📰 General

Trump Backs Saudi Crown Prince Amid Khashoggi Investigation Findings •

President Donald Trump stated in the Oval Office that he was discussing a “very sad subject” regarding the CIA’s assessment of Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman’s involvement in the death of Jamal Khashoggi. The President defended the Saudi Arabian leader, asserting that the CIA’s findings were being considered. He indicated that the intelligence community was examining the situation and that he was aware of the ongoing investigation. Trump’s comments come amidst growing international pressure for accountability regarding the 2018 assassination.

🌍 World

MI5 Warns Chinese Spies Using LinkedIn to Target British Lawmakers •

MI5 has issued a warning to British lawmakers that Chinese intelligence agencies are actively using LinkedIn to identify and target individuals within Parliament. The agency alleges that these operatives are posing as recruiters, attempting to gain access to personnel working within the Houses of Parliament. This follows the recent collapse of a court case involving two British nationals accused of espionage, suggesting a sustained and sophisticated operation. The warning underscores concerns about China’s intelligence activities within the UK’s political system. Authorities are investigating the extent of the targeting and the individuals involved.

🦅 US

Trump’s “Piggy” Remark Sparks Outrage, Renewed Criticism of Attacks on Journalists •

Former President Donald Trump made a derogatory comment, referring to a Bloomberg News reporter as “piggy” during an interaction on Air Force One on Friday. The incident occurred amidst a heated exchange and follows a documented pattern of personal attacks directed at female journalists by Trump. Witnesses reported the exchange took place while Trump was speaking with reporters on the aircraft. This latest incident has reignited concerns about Trump’s rhetoric and its potential impact on the media landscape.

💰 Business

Meta Defeats FTC in Landmark Antitrust Trial Over WhatsApp and Instagram •

Meta has successfully defended itself against an antitrust lawsuit brought by the Federal Trade Commission. Judge James Boasberg ruled that Meta did not engage in anticompetitive practices regarding its acquisitions of WhatsApp and Instagram. The FTC argued that Meta used its dominance in social networking to stifle competition. The court’s decision allows Meta to continue operating its messaging and social media platforms as currently structured.

💻 Technology

Black Friday Early Deals: Top Tech Under $50 Now Available •

Several tech retailers are offering significant discounts on popular accessories ahead of Black Friday. The article highlights a selection of deals currently available, including Anker chargers, Apple AirTags, Blink cameras, and Lego sets. Many of these discounted items represent the lowest prices observed throughout the year. Consumers can purchase these accessories now, capitalizing on early Black Friday promotions.

🎭 Entertainment

Rolling Stone Pays Tribute to Todd Snider, Nashville’s East Nashville Icon •

Rolling Stone recently published a feature honoring the late singer-songwriter Todd Snider, focusing on his significant role within Nashville’s East Nashville music scene. The article recounts a 2007 interview where reporter Mark Anthony Green sought Snider’s perspective on the diverse music scenes of Nashville. Snider was described as a key figure and advocate for East Nashville, a bohemian area known for its independent musicians. The piece highlights Green’s initial interest in Snider’s insights into the city’s musical landscape.

🏅 Sports

Shedeur Sanders’ Home Targeted in $200,000 Property Theft – Deputies Investigate •

Masked individuals burglarized Shedeur Sanders’ Granger Township residence on Sunday, gaining entry through an unlocked door. The thieves absconded with over $200,000 worth of property, according to Medina County Sheriff’s deputies. Authorities are currently investigating the incident and the full extent of the stolen items remains under review. The investigation is ongoing, and no suspects have been apprehended at this time.

🔬 Science

NASA Closely Monitoring Bus-Sized Asteroid on Approach to Earth •

NASA’s Center for Near Earth Object Studies (CNEOS) is tracking an asteroid, designated 2025 VP1, which is currently traveling towards Earth. The asteroid is approximately 37 feet in diameter and moving at a speed of over 18,300 miles per hour. Scientists are assessing the potential risk posed by the object’s trajectory. Current data suggests the asteroid will not impact Earth, but continued observation is ongoing.

🩺 Health

Ethiopia Marburg Outbreak Confirmed Deadly, Global Spread Remains Limited •

Ethiopia has reported three deaths linked to the Marburg virus, prompting concerns but indicating a limited risk of widespread international transmission. The virus, similar to Ebola, is characterized by severe fever, hemorrhagic symptoms, and potential for high mortality rates. Health officials are working to contain the outbreak through contact tracing, isolation, and supportive care for infected individuals. Currently, the outbreak appears isolated to a specific region within Ethiopia, with no confirmed cases reported elsewhere.
